newsitem.title: GERMANY: East to catch W.German building malaise, Ifo says.
newsitem.headline: East to catch W.German building malaise, Ifo says.

text.p: The slump hitting the west German building sector will spread to the eastern states in 1997, causing a two- to three-percent decline in overall German building spending, the Ifo think-tank said on Tuesday.

"The construction industry, which was one of the most important driving forces for Germany's overall economic development after unification, has become a brake on growth," the respected German institute said in a report.
Ifo also predicted a two- to three-percent decline in overall building spending in the current year.

Construction spending in the eastern states, where the industry experienced a boom period after unification, will continue to rise slightly this year while the west will see a sharp decline, Ifo predicted.
However, next year will see the excess availability of expensive new private housing, office buildings and shopping centres hitting the eastern states, Ifo said.

"Spending will rise only slightly this year, also because of output interruptions from the harsh winter, which were even worse than in the west. Next year, we must expect a decline of around four percent," Ifo said.
Building activity and the number of completed houses will drop nationwide in 1996 and 1997, mainly because of decreased spending by individuals and the public sector, Ifo said.
"The number of homes completed, which was over 600,000 in 1995, will drop sharply," Ifo said.
The government's tighter rein on spending had made individuals even more unwilling to invest in housing, Ifo said.
Ifo described as "dubious" plans to introduce a minimum wage for the sector, saying such measures should only be used as temporary aids to help building firms adapt to changing market conditions.

German building unions and employers last week agreed to seek legislation for a minimum hourly wage of 17 marks in west Germany and 15.64 marks in the east in a bid to fend off competition from low-paying foreign rivals.
Weakness in the building sector was a major factor in the slowdown of the entire German economy during the winter months.
But economists are optimistic that output increased in the second quarter of the year and will continue to expand later this year.

Ifo's survey of business developments in the manufacturing sector in July found that conditions for the west German industry as a whole improved in the month, with orders in hand showing an advance for the first time since the start of 1995.
However, east German conditions had remained poor and were not expected to improve in the coming months, Ifo said.
West German retailers experienced a small rise in sales in July while east German retail sales dropped despite the end-of-summer sales period.
East German wholesalers also reported negative developments in July, but their west German counterparts experienced a significant improvement.
